comment: Ep84 England vs DR Congo (R32). Theme 'THE LIONS AND THE LEOPARD' — England = the Three Lions of the crown; DR Congo = the Leopard (Les Leopards) -> Legend 084 = the Three Lions. lines.text: On the crest of a kingdom, three lions have prowled for nine hundred years — the symbol of a nation that gave the world this game, and has chased its return ever since. England, the Three Lions, hungry as ever.
But out of the heart of Africa, along the great river, comes the Leopard — silent, powerful, afraid of nothing. Tonight, the lions meet the leopard.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends — episode eighty-four. England, versus DR Congo. A knockout. Win, or the dream dies right here.
England arrive as one of the giants — the home of football, loaded with world-class talent in every line. DR Congo arrive as the Leopards, fearless and physical, the team no giant wants to face.
England — the Three Lions. Deep, dangerous, and desperate to finally bring it home.

Harry Kane leads the line and wears the armband — the deadliest finisher of his generation. Jude Bellingham drives them on with that fearless big-game swagger. And Bukayo Saka glides down the right with a smile and a sting.
Phil Foden weaves the kind of magic that unlocks any defence. And Declan Rice breaks it all up and starts it all again.
DR Congo — the Leopards. Strong, fast, and utterly without fear of any badge or any name.
Yoane Wissa leads the line with relentless running. Silas flies at defenders with electric pace. And Chancel Mbemba, the captain, is a rock who has tamed the very best.
Cédric Bakambu is a born poacher who smells a goal. And Aaron Wan-Bissaka shuts down the wing with the cleanest tackle in the game.
So here is the riddle. Do the Three Lions finally roar when it matters most? Or does the Leopard pounce and drag another giant into the dark?
And stay with me — because this one turns, late, on a moment of pure belief.
Here is how we see it. DR Congo come out fearless, pressing high, and England are rattled early by the speed and the noise.
The Leopard strikes first. The whole stadium freezes.
And it lands. Cédric Bakambu pounces in the box and finishes ice-cold. DR Congo lead. The Leopard has drawn blood.
But these lions do not lie down. England steady, the quality rises, and Foden begins to pull the strings.
And Harry Kane does what Harry Kane does. He levels it, cool and clinical. One — one. The lions are roaring now.
And then, late, the belief. Jude Bellingham rises in the box and heads it home. Two — one, England. The Three Lions survive the scare.
Two — one. DR Congo were magnificent, and fearless, and so nearly there — but England's lions found a way, the way the great ones do.
Our prediction — England two, DR Congo one. Bellingham, late. Not played yet — the real ninety is yours to watch.
And DR Congo leave with their heads high — the Leopard that terrified a giant, undone only by a single header in the dying minutes.
England march on. The Three Lions, reminding the world that the old kings still have teeth.
So you tell me — the lions, or the leopard? Comment ENGLAND for the Three Lions — comment CONGO for the Leopards of the river.

On the crest of the crown they have stood for nine centuries — three golden lions, guardians of a footballing kingdom, who bow to no one and never stop hunting. Legend eighty-four — the Three Lions, Keepers of the Crown.
The players write the night. But the Three Lions carry one truth — greatness is not never being afraid. It is roaring back the moment the fear arrives.
